newsitem.title: USA: Canada spot natgas eases from highs ahead of wknd.
newsitem.headline: Canada spot natgas eases from highs ahead of wknd.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices backed off of Thursday's year-highs on Friday due to an expected restart of a British Columbia gas plant and a slight warm-up in weekend temperatures in Alberta, sources said.

At Sumas, Wash., the Canada-U.S. export point, gas traded early in the $5.00-5.50 per million British thermal units (mmBtu) range, but prices retreated to about $4.50 and then about $3.50 as more capacity became available from Westcoast.
Westcoast Energy said its McMahon gas processing plant in B.C., which has a capacity of about 650 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd), would resume normal service on Saturday.
More seasonable temperatures in the northwestern U.S. added to the downward pressure.
At the AECO storage hub, prices began around C$2.40 per gigajoule (GJ), then softened to the high-$2.20s, but rebounded late to the mid-C$2.30s.
This compares with Thursday's market in the high-C$2.60s.
December AECO was talked in the high-C$2.20s to mid-C$2.30s, up about 80 cents from November 1, while January prices were seen at C$2.30 and higher.
At Niagara, where colder temperatures are forecast through next week, prices were steady to stronger on the day in the $4.10-4.15 per mmBtu range.

Despite recent reports of extensive storage withdrawals in Alberta, stocks in western Canada were about seven percent above year-ago levels as of November 15, as reported by the Canadian Gas Association (CGA).
In the East, stocks were almost one percent above year-ago levels during the same period, while total Canadian inventories were more than five percent ahead of a year ago.
A decline below year-ago levels may surface in next week's CGA report as bitterly cold temperatures in Alberta forced many buyers to depend on storage this week.
